title: Independiente Medellín vs Cúcuta Face Off in Liga BetPlay
seoTitle: Independiente Medellín vs Cúcuta in Liga BetPlay
subtitle: The match at Atanasio Girardot includes a solidarity drive for earthquake victims and a potential debut for a new signing
excerpt: Independiente Medellín and Cúcuta Deportivo clash in the sixth round of Liga BetPlay, featuring a fundraising effort for earthquake‑displaced residents and a return to.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The showdown between Independiente Medellín and Cúcuta Deportivo in the sixth round of Liga BetPlay is set to energize Colombian football this Saturday at the Atanasio Girardot Stadium. The fixture brings together teams at different stages of the standings and also marks a solidarity mobilisation for those displaced by a recent earthquake.

Independiente Medellín’s Championship Situation

Independiente Medellín sits in third place on the table with 9 points and a +3 goal difference. Under the guidance of coach Luis Amaranto Perea, the side has started with three wins in three matches, scoring seven goals and conceding four across the competition.

The Antioquian club has two fixtures postponed due to the earthquake tragedy: against Millonarios at Atanasio Girardot and against Internacional de Bogotá away. The club also has the possible inclusion of Juan Fernando Quintero, a recent signing, on the field.

Cúcuta Deportivo’s Current Status and Absences

Cúcuta Deportivo arrives for the match in 17th place, having earned just 2 points and a –6 goal difference. With no victories in the tournament, the team has two draws and two defeats, and sits in a relegation‑alert position after conceding nine goals.

The squad has not won an away game all year, recording six draws and nine defeats as visitors. For this encounter, Cúcuta will be without Diego Calcaterra, suspended after receiving a red card in the previous match.

Solidarity Action for Earthquake‑Affected Residents

Before the evening’s fixture, Independiente Medellín will host a solidarity call to fans at the Plaza de Banderas of the Atanasio Girardot sports complex from 3:00 p.m. to 7:30 p.m. The venue will feature a bazaar selling household items, mattresses, cleaning supplies, food, health products, hardware, agricultural goods and pet supplies.

Donations paid by supporters and products handed in on the spot will be forwarded to the Red Cross for distribution to those in need. The program also includes an auction of two jerseys signed by the squad’s players.

Recent Head‑to‑Head Record

The head‑to‑head history shows an unbeaten streak for Independiente Medellín in the last 11 league encounters against Cúcuta, tallying eight wins and three draws. In the six most recent meetings, Medellín scored at least two goals per match.
